title: Welcome to Zillow Preferred

slides.title: How a Zillow lead reaches you
slides.lead: Start with the Follow Up Boss contact record.
slides.body:
Live connection

You are connected with a buyer. Find the matching record before updating it.

Tour request

Read the property and requested time. A request alone is not a confirmed appointment.

Touring alert

Read what happened and what response is needed. Check the existing history.
slides.notes: Use your actual team routing process for the demonstration. Do not assume every notification means the same thing. Confirm access before class. If a login is missing, resolve it or use a named coach observation; do not treat watching the demo as the learner completing the action.
slides.cue: What would tell you that you have the correct record?

slides.title: Start in People
slides.lead: Use the actual contact name, source, and activity to find the record.
slides.notes: Demonstrate People, smart lists, and filtering in your training account. Open the image at full size if labels are hard to see. Ask an agent to point to the source and most recent activity.
slides.cue: Where would you look for a new Zillow contact?

slides.title: Find Avery in the training account
slides.lead: Confirm the source before opening or editing a record.
slides.body:
Find the name

Search for Avery in the training pond.

Check the source

Look for Zillow. If needed, use Filters → Add filter → Lead Source.

Open and confirm

Read the contact details and activity. Make sure this is the right Avery.
slides.notes: Have an agent narrate where they would click. Use the training account, never a live contact as a practice record. The embedded record exercises begin inside a contact. An agent’s written report does not automatically verify People/search navigation. Observe it in the actual training account and record who observed it.

activity.prompt: Find Avery in your training account. Confirm the source, assignment, and recent activity before editing.

fields.label: Where did you find the record? Name the path you used, or the control you need help finding.

slides.title: Check the Details panel
slides.lead: The stage should match what actually happened.
slides.notes: Point out Stage, Assigned, Source, and Timeframe without narrating every control. Timing should come from the buyer, not a guess. Demonstrate the menu and green save check, then let every agent attempt the task. Do not turn intuitive stage names into a quiz.
slides.cue: Which detail would you verify before saving?

slides.title: Practice: save the appointment stage
slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction. This is a separate fictional case. Keep the original FUB controls, save behavior, hints, and server check. Record check passed means the required actions passed, not that note wording or overall readiness was graded. Have the agent reopen and verify the saved changes.
slides.cue: Make the update, save it, then check your work.

activity.prompt: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.

slides.title: Write what the next agent needs
slides.lead: Record what happened, what the buyer said, and the agreed next step.
slides.body:
“Spoke with Avery. Looking for three bedrooms in Tacoma in 60–90 days. I’ll send two homes on Thursday, then call to compare them.”

Keep the facts

Use the buyer’s words where they clarify a need.

Make the next step specific

Name the action and agreed date.

Leave out guesses

A friendly conversation is not proof of readiness or budget.
slides.notes: Ask what the example tells the next caller. Then complete the note exercise. Coach one missing fact rather than rewriting the entire note for the agent. Keep source, assignment, and history in view. Background information suggests a question; it does not establish finances, family circumstances, timing, or readiness. The note check measures saving an action, not writing quality.
slides.cue: Could someone follow up using only this note?

slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction. This is a separate fictional case. slides.title: Give the follow-up a date and time
slides.lead: Write an action you will recognize when it comes due.
slides.body:
History versus next action

The note says what happened. The task schedules what happens next.

Make it usable

Call Avery to compare 406 and 422 Juniper — Thursday, 3 p.m.

Before you leave

Save a real date and time, then reopen and verify it.
slides.notes: Explain the difference between a note and a task. The note records history; the task schedules the next action. Complete the missed-call exercise next.
slides.cue: What makes a task usable tomorrow?

slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction. This is a separate fictional case. Keep the original FUB controls, save behavior, hints, and server check. Record check passed means the required actions passed, not that note wording or overall readiness was graded. slides.title: Nurture needs a conversation
slides.lead: Compare two situations. Explain the evidence, next action, and review point.
slides.body:
Case A · Later timeline, still engaged

The buyer expects to move later and continues replying and discussing homes.

Case B · The record went quiet

The buyer has not responded recently. The record needs a review of what happened and what is due next.
slides.notes: Give everyone two minutes to write before discussing. Compare two contrasting responses, then explain the team’s actual nurture rule and why it applies. Do not invent a timeline, assume silence means nurture, or impose a follow-up standard beyond the doctrine’s first-week rule. There is no automatic grade. Review the evidence and preserve an owned next action.
slides.cue: What evidence changes your decision, and what still needs to happen?

activity.prompt: Compare the engaged, later-timeline buyer with the record that went quiet.

fields.label: For each case, what evidence would you need before moving this lead to nurture?
What next action would remain, and who owns it?
When would you review the record again?

slides.title: Repair Avery’s record
slides.lead: Only a request to compare homes is confirmed. The record says Appointment set.
slides.body:
What happened

Avery asked to compare 406 and 422 Juniper on Thursday. No appointment was booked.

Read the actual record

Inspect the original record. Compare the saved details with what the buyer actually said. Name the changes before editing.
slides.notes: Give one minute to inspect without solving it for the agent. The next original exercise requires the learner to name the changes before editing. Do not bypass its diagnosis step; discuss the evidence after the learner attempts it.
slides.cue: What would you fix first, and why?

slides.title: Check the record before moving on
slides.body:
Stage

Does it match the event, and did the change save?

Note

Does it explain what happened without guessing?

Task

Is the next action scheduled for a real date and time?

Handoff

Could another agent act on this record without asking you to explain it?
slides.notes: Ask agents to check their own work. Introduce the deal exercise: once an offer is accepted, update the stage and record the deal details.
slides.cue: Which check would catch an unsaved stage?

slides.title: Practice adding a deal
slides.lead: Use the buyer’s name, price, and expected close date.
slides.notes: Demonstrate the deal form, then let the learner enter it. Use fictional details.
slides.cue: What would you check before creating this deal?

slides.title: Practice: record the accepted offer
slides.lead: Update the stage and add the deal from the scenario.
slides.notes: Check the accepted-offer exercise. A passed check should explain the evidence, not just display a result. This is a separate fictional case. Keep the original FUB controls, save behavior, hints, and server check. Record check passed means the required actions passed, not that note wording or overall readiness was graded. Have the agent reopen and verify the saved changes.
slides.cue: What changed after the offer was accepted?

activity.prompt: Update the stage and add the deal from the scenario.

slides.title: Where will you start tomorrow?
slides.lead: Use your tasks and new leads to plan the next calls.
slides.body:
Due tasks

Review what you agreed to do and when.

New leads

Find the correct contact and read the history.

After each conversation

Update the stage, note, and dated next task.
slides.notes: Give 30 seconds without notes. Then ask partners to compare. Revisit only the missing item, not the entire lesson.
slides.cue: Explain your first five minutes in Follow Up Boss.

activity.prompt: Use your tasks and new leads to plan the next calls.

fields.label: Without looking back: what belongs in a useful contact record?

slides.title: Before your next client conversation
slides.lead: Write down when you will practice again.
slides.body:
After each conversation

Save the true stage, factual note, and dated next action before moving on.

With your coach

Review a real record together after the next relevant client conversation.
slides.notes: In live sessions, closing the session creates 24-hour recall, three-day fresh-case, and seven-day coach-review assignments. Confirm each agent’s named coach and session timezone. Agents see due work in Rep; the daily digest links to due or reviewable work. In self-paced study, arrange these checks with a coach. Without a relevant client opportunity, use a fresh fictional case and label real-work application not yet observed. Practice readiness is separate from quiz certification and activation.
slides.cue: Tell your partner what you will practice and when.

activity.prompt: Make the record update part of finishing the conversation.

fields.label: After my next call, I will complete ___ before moving on.
My next follow-up block starts in ___.
My named coach and the example we will review.

resources:
Live sessions

Sign in to your assigned session. Submit answers to your presenter; unsubmitted text remains private. If the presenter moves on, finish the current activity and use Return to presenter to catch up.

Practice again

Complete your 24-hour recall, three-day fresh case, and seven-day coaching review in Rep. In self-paced study, arrange these checks with a coach.

What completion means

A record check is evidence of saved actions. Observed practice, coach readiness, quiz certification, and activation are separate.
